description.ncbi_summary: This gene encodes a member of a family of enzymes that function to add glutathione to target electrophilic compounds, including carcinogens, therapeutic drugs, environmental toxins, and products of oxidative stress. This action is an important step in detoxification of these compounds. This subfamily of enzymes has a particular role in protecting cells from reactive oxygen species and the products of peroxidation. Polymorphisms in this gene influence the ability of individuals to metabolize different drugs. This gene is located in a cluster of similar genes and pseudogenes on chromosome 6. Alternative splicing results in multiple transcript variants. [provided by RefSeq, Jan 2016].

uniprot_function.text: Glutathione S-transferase involved in the clearance of a variety of electrophilic toxic compounds by glutathione conjugation, including harmful products generated during oxidative stress and xenobiotics such as environmental toxins, drugs, and carcinogens including derivatives of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PubMed:12067250). Catalyzes the nucleophilic attack of the sulfur atom of glutathione on the electrophilic groups of a wide range of substrates (PubMed:20606271, PubMed:9084911). Involved in the formation of glutathione conjugates of both prostaglandin A2 (PGA2) and prostaglandin J2 (PGJ2) (PubMed:9084911). Also catalyzes the isomerization of D5-androstene-3,17-dione (AD) into D4-androstene-3,17-dione and may therefore play an important role in hormone biosynthesis (PubMed:11152686). Involved in the protection from oxidative stress through its glutathione-dependent peroxidase activity toward lipid hydroperoxides, including linoleic acid hydroperoxides, dilinoleoyl phosphatidylcholine hydroperoxide, and dilinoleoyl phosphatidylethanolamine hydroperoxide (PubMed:10395737, PubMed:16624487). Can also catalyze glutathione conjugation with 4-hydroxynonenal (4-HNE), a toxic product of lipid peroxidation (PubMed:10395737). In vitro, it catalyzes the reduction of cumene hydroperoxide (PubMed:10395737).
